title: Jam Roly-Poly
subtitle: Steamed suet pudding rolled with strawberry jam
excerpt: A suet pastry dough spread with raspberry jam, rolled up, and steamed until dense and comforting. A proper school dinner pudding, best served with a generous pour of custard.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jam roly-poly is one of the defining British school dinner puddings. It was widely served in school canteens throughout the 20th century, earning it the nickname 'dead man's arm' or 'dead man's leg' from generations of schoolchildren for its rolled, sausage-like appearance. The pudding consists of a simple suet dough spread with jam and steamed rather than baked, which gives it a characteristically dense, damp texture. Some versions are baked, giving a slightly crisper exterior. The traditional jam is raspberry but strawberry or mixed fruit jam work equally well. The pudding must be served with custard; without it, the dense suet pastry is too heavy. It reheats well by steaming again for 20 minutes.

recipeTools.notes: A large pan to steam the pudding.

content.text: Handle the suet pastry as little as possible: overworking develops gluten and makes it tough. Roll it into a rectangle about 1 cm thick. Spread the jam to within 2 cm of the edges, then roll tightly from the shorter end. Wrap securely in greased baking paper and then foil, twisting the ends closed like a Christmas cracker. The parcel must be suspended above the water level in the pan; it should steam, not boil.
Mix the flour, suet, sugar, and salt in a bowl. Add the milk and mix with a knife, then bring together with your hands until a soft dough forms. Do not overwork.
On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a rectangle about 25 x 30 cm and 1 cm thick. Spread the jam over the surface, leaving a 2 cm border all around.
Roll up tightly from the shorter end. Pinch the ends to seal. Place onto buttered baking paper and roll up, twisting the ends closed. Wrap again in a layer of foil, twisting the ends.

Place a trivet or upturned saucer in a large pan. Pour in 5 cm of boiling water. Set the pudding on the trivet. Cover and steam for 1 hour 30 minutes, checking the water level every 30 minutes and topping up as needed. Unwrap carefully and serve in thick slices with hot custard.
